How to remove metadata from a PDF

Every PDF carries information about who made it and with what software. Here is what is inside, why it matters and how to strip it without uploading your file anywhere.

Updated 2026-11-07 · 4 min read
Clean your files in secondsFree, no sign-up, and everything runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
Open IA Cleaner

What metadata does a PDF contain?

  • Document Info: Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Creator (the app that made the original, e.g. Word) and Producer (the PDF engine), plus creation and modification dates.
  • XMP metadata: an XML block that can repeat all of the above and add much more — editing history, tool names and, increasingly, AI-related tags.
  • Page-level data and attachments, including C2PA provenance manifests in newer files.

These fields can reveal your name, your company, the software you used (including AI writing or design tools) and when you worked on the file.

How to remove PDF metadata with IA Cleaner

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Images & documents.
  2. Drop your PDF. The report lists every field found — Author, Creator, Producer, XMP — and flags AI-related values.
  3. Click Download to get the cleaned copy.

The PDF is rewritten from scratch, so the old values are not left behind in the file. Password-protected PDFs can’t be modified — remove the password first.

Other ways

  • Adobe Acrobat Pro: Tools → Redact → Sanitize Document removes hidden information (paid).
  • Microsoft Word, before exporting: File → Info → Check for Issues → Inspect Document, then in the PDF export options untick Document properties.
  • ExifTool: exiftool -all:all= file.pdf. Note that ExifTool edits PDFs incrementally, so the original metadata can still be recovered unless you rewrite the file afterwards (for example with qpdf).

Don’t forget the content

Metadata is only part of the story: comments, tracked changes, hidden layers or text covered by black boxes can still be in the file. Clean the original document before exporting, and use proper redaction for sensitive text.
